screens.title: What You Will Learn
screens.html:
This lesson is about graphs of straight lines and the equations behind them. On the GED, you will read graphs, find how fast something changes, write the equation of a line, and use function notation. A few ideas, especially slope and the y-intercept, unlock almost every question.

Work through one screen at a time. Most screens teach one idea, show a worked example, and end with a check you answer before moving on. Keep graph paper and a pencil nearby and sketch as you go.

By the end, you will be able to:

  • Read and plot points in all four quadrants.
  • Find slope from two points, a graph, a table, or an equation, and explain it as a rate of change.
  • Find intercepts and write equations of lines, including parallel and perpendicular lines.
  • Use function notation and decide whether a relation is a function.
  • Read real-world graphs and compare functions.

screens.title: The Coordinate Plane
screens.html:
The coordinate plane is made of two number lines. The x-axis runs left and right. The y-axis runs up and down. They cross at the origin, (0, 0).

Every point has an address called an ordered pair, (x, y). The order matters:

Across first, then up or down. The x-coordinate tells you how far to move left (negative) or right (positive). The y-coordinate tells you how far to move down (negative) or up (positive).

The point (5, 2) and the point (2, 5) are different places. Mixing up the order is the most common graphing mistake.

steps: Start at the origin. The x-coordinate is −2, so move 2 units left.
The y-coordinate is 4, so from there move 4 units up.
example.answer: The point is 2 left and 4 up from the origin, marked A on the graph.

check.why: The most common wrong click is (3, −4), which comes from moving up or down first. Move across first: 4 left, then 3 up.
check.hint: Start at the origin. Which way does the first number tell you to move?
check.explain:
The x-coordinate is −4: move 4 units left.

The y-coordinate is 3: move 3 units up.

The point is (−4, 3), in the upper left. If you clicked (3, −4), you switched the order of the coordinates.

screens.title: Quadrants
screens.html:
The axes divide the plane into four quadrants, numbered I, II, III, IV counterclockwise, starting at the upper right. The signs of the coordinates tell you the quadrant.

QuadrantLocationSigns
Iupper right(+, +)
IIupper left(−, +)
IIIlower left(−, −)
IVlower right(+, −)

A point with a 0 coordinate, such as (0, −5) or (3, 0), sits on an axis and is not in any quadrant.

steps: x = 6 is positive: the point is to the right of the y-axis.
y = −1 is negative: the point is below the x-axis.

check.prompt:
Choose the quadrant for each point.

(−6, −1) is in Quadrant {{0}}.

(−2, 7) is in Quadrant {{1}}.

why: Quadrant I is (+, +). Both coordinates here are negative, so the point is to the left and below: Quadrant III.
Quadrant II has a positive y-coordinate. Here y = −1 is negative, so the point is below the x-axis.
Quadrant IV has a positive x-coordinate. Here x = −6, so the point is to the left of the y-axis.
Quadrant I needs a positive x. Here x = −2, so the point is left of the y-axis.
Quadrant III has a negative y. Here y = 7 is positive, so the point is above the x-axis.
You may have switched the signs. Quadrant IV is (+, −), but this point is (−, +): left and up, which is Quadrant II.

check.hint: Look at the sign of each coordinate. Negative x means left; negative y means down.
check.explain:
(−6, −1): x is negative (left) and y is negative (down). Left and down is Quadrant III.

(−2, 7): x is negative (left) and y is positive (up). Left and up is Quadrant II.

Remember that the quadrants are numbered counterclockwise starting at the upper right.

screens.title: Slope from a Graph
screens.html:
Slope tells you how steep a line is and which way it goes. It is the rise (vertical change) divided by the run (horizontal change).

slope = rise / run

To find the slope from a graph:

  1. Pick two points where the line crosses grid corners exactly.
  2. Count the run, moving to the right.
  3. Count the rise: up is positive, down is negative.
  4. Divide rise by run and simplify.

Read lines from left to right. A line that goes uphill has a positive slope; a line that goes downhill has a negative slope.

example.prompt: Find the slope of the line shown.
steps: The line passes through grid corners at (0, 1) and (3, 3).
Run: from x = 0 to x = 3 is 3 to the right. Rise: from y = 1 to y = 3 is 2 up.
example.answer: The slope is 2/3. The line rises, so positive makes sense.

check.prompt: What is the slope of the line shown? Enter a fraction or a decimal.

mistakes.why: The size is right, but the line falls from left to right, so the slope is negative: −3/2.
You divided the run by the rise. The rise goes on top: down 3 over right 2 is −3/2.
2 is the y-intercept, where the line crosses the y-axis. The slope is rise over run: −3/2.

check.hint: Use the two marked points. Count the run to the right first, then how far down the line goes.
check.explain:
The marked points are (0, 2) and (2, −1).

Run: from x = 0 to x = 2 is 2 to the right.

Rise: from y = 2 to y = −1 is 3 down, so the rise is −3.

Slope = −3 / 2 = −3/2 (or −1.5).

The line falls from left to right, so a negative slope makes sense. If you got 3/2, you dropped the sign.

screens.title: The Slope Formula
screens.html:
When you have two points but no graph, use the slope formula. It is on the GED formula sheet.

m = (y2 − y1) / (x2 − x1)

  • The letter m stands for slope.
  • The y-values go on top; the x-values go on the bottom.
  • Subtract in the same order on top and bottom. Either point can be point 1.
  • Subtracting a negative means adding: 4 − (−2) = 6.

example.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (−1, 6) and (3, −2).
steps: Change in y: −2 − 6 = −8. Change in x: 3 − (−1) = 4.

check.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (−3, 5) and (1, −7).

mistakes.why: You may have subtracted in a different order on top and bottom. Keep the same order: (−7 − 5) / (1 − (−3)) = −12/4 = −3.
You put the change in x on top. Slope is change in y over change in x: −12/4 = −3.
You treated 1 − (−3) as 1 − 3 = −2. Subtracting a negative means adding: 1 − (−3) = 4, and −12/4 = −3.

check.hint: Label the points first. Change in y goes on top.
check.explain:
Let (x1, y1) = (−3, 5) and (x2, y2) = (1, −7).

Change in y: −7 − 5 = −12

Change in x: 1 − (−3) = 1 + 3 = 4

m = −12 / 4 = −3

The most common slip is writing 1 − (−3) as −2.

screens.title: Zero and Undefined Slope
screens.html:
Two kinds of lines have special slopes.

  • A horizontal line has no rise. Its slope is 0 / run = 0. Its equation looks like y = −2: every point has the same y-value.
  • A vertical line has no run. Its slope would be rise / 0, and you cannot divide by zero, so the slope is undefined. Its equation looks like x = 3: every point has the same x-value.

Do not mix these up. 0 on the top of the fraction means slope 0. 0 on the bottom means undefined.

steps: Change in y: −1 − 5 = −6. Change in x: 3 − 3 = 0.
example.answer: The slope is undefined. The line is the vertical line x = 3, the dark line on the graph.

check.prompt:
The line through (−2, 4) and (6, 4) has slope {{0}}.

The line through (1, 8) and (1, −3) has slope {{1}}.

why: You switched the two special cases. The y-values match, so the rise is 0 and the slope is 0 / 8 = 0. Undefined is for vertical lines.
8 is the run, 6 − (−2). The rise is 4 − 4 = 0, and 0 / 8 = 0.
You may have put the run in the denominator under a rise of 1. The rise is 0, so the slope is 0.
You switched the two special cases. The x-values match, so the run is 0. Dividing by 0 is impossible, so the slope is undefined.
−11 is the rise, −3 − 8. You still have to divide by the run, which is 1 − 1 = 0, and that cannot be done.
11 is the size of the rise. The run is 1 − 1 = 0, so the slope is undefined.

check.hint: Find the change in y and the change in x for each pair. Which one is 0?
check.explain:
First line: the y-values are both 4, so the rise is 0. Slope = 0 / (6 − (−2)) = 0/8 = 0. It is the horizontal line y = 4.

Second line: the x-values are both 1, so the run is 0. Slope = (−3 − 8) / 0, which cannot be computed, so the slope is undefined. It is the vertical line x = 1.

screens.title: Slope as a Rate of Change
screens.html:
In real life, slope is a rate of change: how much the output changes for each one unit of input. Its units are “output units per input unit,” such as dollars per hour or miles per gallon.

To find the rate from a table, pick two rows and divide:

rate = change in output / change in input

If the input goes up by more than 1 between rows, you must divide by that jump. If hours go 0, 2, 4 and the cost goes up $40 each row, the rate is $40 / 2 = $20 per hour, not $40.

A negative rate means the quantity is going down, such as water draining or a balance being paid off.

example.prompt: A car's gas tank holds 14 gallons after 60 miles and 11 gallons after 150 miles. What is the rate of change?
steps: Change in gallons: 11 − 14 = −3. Change in miles: 150 − 60 = 90.
example.answer: −1/30 gallon per mile: the car uses 1 gallon every 30 miles.

check.skill: Rate of change from a table
check.prompt:
A printer's output is shown in the table.

Minutes36912
Pages printed75150225300

At what rate does the printer print, in pages per minute?

mistakes.why: 75 is the change in pages between rows, but the minutes go up by 3 each row. Divide: 75 / 3 = 25 pages per minute.
You divided minutes by pages. The rate asked for is pages per minute, so pages go on top: 75 / 3 = 25.

check.hint: Find how many pages are added from one row to the next, and how many minutes pass.
check.explain:
From 3 minutes to 6 minutes, pages go from 75 to 150.

Rate = (150 − 75) / (6 − 3) = 75 / 3 = 25 pages per minute.

Check with the last two rows: (300 − 225) / (12 − 9) = 75 / 3 = 25. The answer 75 forgets that 3 minutes pass between rows.

screens.title: Intercepts
screens.html:
An intercept is where a graph crosses an axis.

  • The y-intercept is where the line crosses the y-axis. Every point on the y-axis has x = 0, so set x = 0 and solve for y. Write it as (0, b).
  • The x-intercept is where the line crosses the x-axis. Every point on the x-axis has y = 0, so set y = 0 and solve for x. Write it as (a, 0).

In a word problem, the y-intercept is usually a starting amount, and the x-intercept is often the moment something runs out or reaches zero.

steps: x-intercept: y = 0 gives 0 = 2x − 6, so 2x = 6 and x = 3. Point (3, 0).

check.prompt: The line y = 3x − 12 crosses the x-axis at the point (a, 0). What is a?

mistakes.why: −12 is the y-intercept, found by setting x = 0. For the x-intercept, set y = 0: 0 = 3x − 12, so x = 4.
From 0 = 3x − 12, add 12 to both sides: 3x = 12, so x = +4. You may have moved the 12 without changing its sign.

check.hint: On the x-axis, y = 0. Replace y with 0 and solve for x.
check.explain:
Set y = 0: 0 = 3x − 12.

Add 12 to both sides: 12 = 3x.

Divide by 3: x = 4. The x-intercept is (4, 0).

Check: 3(4) − 12 = 0. If you answered −12, you found the y-intercept instead.

screens.title: Slope-Intercept Form: y = mx + b
screens.html:
The most useful form of a line is slope-intercept form:

y = mx + b   m = slope    b = y-intercept

You can read both numbers straight from the equation. In y = −4x + 9, the slope is −4 and the y-intercept is (0, 9). Watch the signs: in y = 5x − 2, b is −2.

To graph y = mx + b: plot the y-intercept (0, b). Then use the slope as rise over run to step to a second point. Draw the line through both.

steps: Slope 3/4: from (0, −2) go up 3 and right 4 to (4, 1).

check.prompt: The line y = −(2/3)x + 1 is shown. Click the point on the line that has an x-coordinate of 3.
check.why: The most common wrong click is (3, 3), which comes from going up 2 instead of down 2. A negative slope means the line goes down as you move right.
check.hint: Start at the y-intercept (0, 1). The slope −2/3 means down 2 for every 3 to the right.
check.explain:
The y-intercept is (0, 1).

The slope −2/3 means down 2, right 3. From (0, 1), move right 3 to x = 3 and down 2 to y = −1.

Check: −(2/3)(3) + 1 = −2 + 1 = −1. The point is (3, −1).

If you clicked (3, 3), you moved up instead of down.

screens.title: From Standard Form to y = mx + b
screens.html:
Some equations come in standard form: Ax + By = C, such as 2x + 3y = 12. To find the slope, solve for y:

  1. Move the x-term to the other side (change its sign).
  2. Divide every term by the number in front of y.

The intercepts are quick in standard form: set x = 0 to find the y-intercept, and set y = 0 to find the x-intercept.

Divide every term. From 4x + 2y = 10, you get 2y = −4x + 10, then y = −2x + 5, not y = −4x + 5.

example.prompt: Find the slope and both intercepts of 2x + 3y = 12.

check.prompt: What is the slope of the line 3x + 4y = 8? Enter a fraction or a decimal.

mistakes.why: You moved 3x across but did not divide it by 4. Divide every term: 4y = −3x + 8 gives y = −(3/4)x + 2.
When 3x moves to the other side, it becomes −3x. The slope is −3/4.
The fraction is upside down. Divide the x-coefficient by the y-coefficient: −3/4.

check.hint: Solve for y. Move the x-term, then divide every term by 4.
check.explain:
Subtract 3x from both sides: 4y = −3x + 8.

Divide every term by 4: y = −(3/4)x + 2.

The slope is −3/4 (or −0.75).

Check with intercepts: (0, 2) and (8/3, 0); slope = (0 − 2)/(8/3 − 0) = −2 × 3/8 = −3/4.

screens.title: Writing the Equation of a Line
screens.html:
To write the equation of a line, you need the slope and one point.

Point-slope form (on the formula sheet): y − y1 = m(x − x1)

Method for two points:

  1. Find the slope with the slope formula.
  2. Put the slope and either point into point-slope form, or into y = mx + b and solve for b.
  3. Simplify to y = mx + b.
  4. Check with the other point.

Careful with signs: with the point (−4, 2), point-slope form is y − 2 = m(x + 4), because x − (−4) = x + 4.

example.prompt: Write the equation of the line through (−4, −1) and (4, 5).

check.prompt: Which equation represents the line through (1, 4) and (3, 10)?
why: You used the y-value of the first point, 4, as the y-intercept. But (1, 4) is not on the y-axis. Solve 4 = 3(1) + b to get b = 1.
You wrote point-slope form as y + 4 = 3(x − 1). It should be y − 4 = 3(x − 1), which simplifies to y = 3x + 1.
You put the change in x over the change in y. The slope is (10 − 4)/(3 − 1) = 6/2 = 3, not 1/3.
check.hint: Find the slope first. Then substitute one point into y = mx + b to find b.
check.explain:
Slope: (10 − 4) / (3 − 1) = 6 / 2 = 3.

Use (1, 4): 4 = 3(1) + b, so b = 1.

The equation is y = 3x + 1. Check (3, 10): 3(3) + 1 = 10. Correct.

The equation y = 3x + 4 is tempting, but 4 is the y-value at x = 1, not at x = 0.

screens.title: Writing a Linear Model from Words
screens.html:
Many GED problems describe a line in words. Look for two numbers:

  • The rate (slope): words like per, each, every. It multiplies the variable.
  • The starting value (y-intercept): words like fee, initial, starting, already. It is added on.

For example, a gym charges a $35 sign-up fee plus $20 per month. The cost after m months is C = 20m + 35.

If something is decreasing, the rate is negative. The x-intercept then tells you when the amount reaches zero.

example.prompt: A phone card starts with $30 and loses $0.15 per minute of calls. Write a model and find the balance after 80 minutes.
steps: Rate: −0.15 dollars per minute. Starting value: 30.

check.prompt: A tank holds 500 gallons of water. It drains at a steady 25 gallons per minute, so the amount left after t minutes is W = −25t + 500. After how many minutes is the tank empty?

mistakes.why: Time cannot be negative here. From 0 = −25t + 500, add 25t to both sides: 25t = 500, so t = 20.
You multiplied 500 by 25. The tank loses 25 gallons each minute, so divide: 500 / 25 = 20 minutes.

check.hint: Empty means W = 0. Set the equation equal to 0 and solve for t.
check.explain:
Empty means W = 0: 0 = −25t + 500.

Add 25t to both sides: 25t = 500.

Divide by 25: t = 20 minutes.

This is the x-intercept of the graph, the point (20, 0).

screens.title: Parallel and Perpendicular Slopes
screens.html:
• Parallel lines never meet. They have the same slope and different y-intercepts. Example: y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x − 7.
  • Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle. Their slopes are opposite reciprocals: flip the fraction and change the sign. The two slopes multiply to −1.
SlopePerpendicular slope
2/3−3/2
−41/4
1−1

A horizontal line (slope 0) and a vertical line (undefined slope) are also perpendicular.

example.prompt: Are y = (2/5)x + 3 and y = −(5/2)x − 1 parallel, perpendicular, or neither?

check.prompt: What is the slope of a line perpendicular to y = (4/5)x − 2? Enter a fraction or a decimal.

mistakes.why: 4/5 is the slope of a parallel line. Perpendicular slopes are opposite reciprocals: flip and change the sign.
You flipped the fraction but kept the sign. (4/5)(5/4) = 1, not −1. Change the sign too: −5/4.
You changed the sign but did not flip the fraction. (4/5)(−4/5) is not −1. Flip it too: −5/4.

check.hint: Flip the fraction and change the sign. Check that the two slopes multiply to −1.
check.explain:
The given slope is 4/5.

Flip it: 5/4. Change the sign: −5/4.

Check: (4/5)(−5/4) = −20/20 = −1. Correct.

screens.title: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines Through a Point
screens.html:
A common GED question gives you a line and a point and asks for a new line that is parallel or perpendicular to the first one and passes through the point.

  1. Get the new slope: the same slope for parallel; the opposite reciprocal for perpendicular.
  2. Substitute the point into y = mx + b and solve for b.
  3. Write the equation and check the point.

The y-intercept of the given line does not carry over. Only its slope matters.

example.prompt: Write the line through (2, 3) perpendicular to y = 4x − 1.

check.prompt:
Write the equation of the line that is parallel to y = −3x + 5 and passes through (2, 1).

y = ___   (Type only the right side, such as 5x − 1.)

mistakes.why: That is the given line itself. It does not pass through (2, 1): −3(2) + 5 = −1. Keep the slope and solve 1 = −3(2) + b for a new b.
From 1 = −6 + b, add 6 to both sides: b = 7. You may have subtracted 6 instead.
You used the perpendicular slope, 1/3. Parallel lines have the same slope, −3.

check.hint: Parallel means the same slope, −3. Substitute x = 2 and y = 1 into y = −3x + b and solve for b.
check.explain:
Parallel lines have the same slope, so m = −3.

Substitute (2, 1): 1 = −3(2) + b, so 1 = −6 + b.

Add 6: b = 7.

The equation is y = −3x + 7.

Check: −3(2) + 7 = 1. Correct. Keeping the intercept 5 would give the original line, not a parallel one.

screens.title: What Is a Function?
screens.html:
A function is a rule that gives exactly one output for each input. The input is usually x and the output is y.

  • Lists and tables: if any x-value appears twice with different y-values, it is not a function. Repeated y-values are fine.
  • Graphs: use the vertical line test. If any vertical line touches the graph more than once, it is not a function.

Every non-vertical line is a function. A vertical line, such as x = 4, is not: the input 4 has infinitely many outputs.

Think of people and birthdays. Two people can share a birthday (repeated output), but one person cannot have two birthdays (one input, two outputs).

steps: Look for repeated inputs: x = 2 appears twice.
It is paired with 5 and with 8, two different outputs.

why: Every input (2, 4, 6) is different, so this is a function. The repeated output 3 is allowed.
Every input (−1, 0, 1) is different, so this is a function. Two inputs sharing the output 0 is allowed.
Every input (5, 6, 7) appears once with one output, so this is a function.
check.hint: Look only at the x-values. Is any x-value paired with two different y-values?
check.explain:
In {(1, 2), (2, 4), (1, 6)}, the input 1 is paired with both 2 and 6. One input, two outputs: not a function.

The other three relations never repeat an x-value. Repeated y-values, such as the three 3s, do not break the rule.

screens.title: Function Notation
screens.html:
f(x) is read “f of x.” It means the output of the function f when the input is x. It does not mean f times x.

  • To find f(3), replace every x with 3 (use parentheses) and compute.
  • f(3) = 10 means the point (3, 10) is on the graph.
  • To find x when f(x) = 10, set the expression equal to 10 and solve.

Other letters work the same way: g(x), h(t), C(m).

Put a negative input in parentheses: if f(x) = x2, then f(−3) = (−3)2 = 9, not −9.

example.answer: h(−3) = 17, so (−3, 17) is on the graph.

mistakes.why: You squared −2 as −4. With parentheses, (−2)<sup>2</sup> = 4, so 3(4) − 2(−2) = 12 + 4 = 16.
You computed −2(−2) as −4. A negative times a negative is positive: 12 + 4 = 16.
You multiplied 3 by −2 before squaring: (−6)<sup>2</sup> = 36. Exponents come first: 3(−2)<sup>2</sup> = 3(4) = 12.

check.hint: Replace each x with (−2). Do the exponent before multiplying by 3.

screens.title: Reading Real-World Graphs
screens.html:
Before you answer a question about a graph, read the title and both axis labels, including units. Then read the graph from left to right like a story.

  • Rising: the quantity is increasing.
  • Flat: no change (slope 0).
  • Falling: the quantity is decreasing.
  • Steeper: faster change.

The rate of change over any stretch is the slope: change in the vertical value divided by change in the horizontal value. Be careful when the horizontal axis jumps by more than 1.

example.prompt: Using the graph, describe day 1 to day 3.
steps: From day 1 to day 3, the water rises from 10 to 40 gallons.
example.answer: The barrel gained water at 15 gallons per day, probably from rain.

check.skill: Rate of change from a graph
check.prompt: Use the rain barrel graph. What was the rate of change of the water from day 4 to day 6, in gallons per day?

mistakes.why: −20 is the total change over two days. Divide by the 2 days: −20 / 2 = −10 gallons per day.
The water level fell from 40 to 20, so the rate is negative: −10 gallons per day.

check.hint: Find the change in water and divide by the number of days. Is the water going up or down?
check.explain:
Day 4: 40 gallons. Day 6: 20 gallons.

Rate = (20 − 40) / (6 − 4) = −20 / 2 = −10 gallons per day.

The rate is negative because the water was being used or leaking out.

screens.title: Comparing Functions
screens.html:
The GED often shows two functions in different ways: one as an equation, another as a table, graph, or description. To compare them, change each one into the same two numbers:

  • Rate of change (slope)
  • Starting value (y-intercept: the output when x = 0)

For a table, compute the slope between two rows. If the table does not include x = 0, work backward using the rate.

When two linear functions are equal, their graphs cross. Set the two expressions equal and solve to find where.

example.prompt: Plan A costs C = 15m + 60. Plan B costs $25, $50, $75 for 1, 2, 3 months. When are they equal?
steps: Plan B: rate 25, start 0, so C = 25m.

check.prompt:
Function A is y = 3x + 8. Function B is linear and is shown in the table.

x024
y−1715

{{0}} has the greater rate of change, and {{1}} has the greater y-intercept.

why: Function A's rate is 3. Function B's rate is (7 − (−1)) / (2 − 0) = 8/2 = 4, which is greater.
Function B's y-intercept is −1 (its y-value at x = 0). Function A's is 8, which is greater.

check.hint: Find the slope and the y-value at x = 0 for each function.
check.explain:
Function A: rate 3, y-intercept 8.

Function B: rate (7 − (−1)) / (2 − 0) = 8 / 2 = 4; at x = 0, y = −1, so the y-intercept is −1.

Rate: 4 > 3, so Function B has the greater rate. Y-intercept: 8 > −1, so Function A has the greater y-intercept.

If you read B's rate as 8, you forgot to divide by the change in x, 2.

screens.title: Summary
screens.html:
• (x, y): across first, then up or down. Quadrants I to IV go counterclockwise from the upper right.
  • Slope m = (y2 − y1) / (x2 − x1) = rise / run. Subtract in the same order on top and bottom.
  • Rising: positive. Falling: negative. Horizontal: 0. Vertical: undefined.
  • In context, slope is a rate (“per”). From a table, divide by the change in x.
  • y-intercept: set x = 0. x-intercept: set y = 0.
  • y = mx + b: m is the slope, b is the y-intercept. Point-slope: y − y1 = m(x − x1).
  • Standard form Ax + By = C: solve for y and divide every term.
  • Parallel: same slope. Perpendicular: opposite reciprocals (product −1).
  • A function has exactly one output for each input. f(3) is the output when x = 3.
  • Compare functions by their rates and starting values.

Next: Practice Set A. If you score under 80%, practice the same skills again with Set B. Then take the Exit Check.

items.prompt: Four points are shown on the coordinate plane. Which point has coordinates (−3, 2)?
why: Point A is (3, −2). Both signs are reversed: (−3, 2) means 3 to the left and 2 up.
Point C is (2, −3). That point switches the order of the numbers and both signs. Move across first: 3 left, then 2 up.
Point D is (−2, 3). It comes from moving up 3 and left 2, which switches the order of the coordinates. Move across first (x), then up or down (y).
items.hint: The first number tells you how far to move left or right. The second tells you how far to move up or down.
items.explain:
Start at the origin (0, 0).

The x-coordinate is −3: move 3 units left.

The y-coordinate is 2: move 2 units up.

That location is Point B, in Quadrant II.

Point D is (−2, 3): it comes from moving up 3 and left 2, which switches the order of the coordinates. Point A is (3, −2), which has both signs reversed.

items.prompt: Find the slope of the line that passes through (−6, 4) and (3, −2). Enter a fraction or a decimal.

mistakes.why: You put the change in x on top. Slope is change in y over change in x: −6/9 = −2/3.
The line falls from (−6, 4) down to (3, −2), so the slope must be negative. Check that you subtracted in the same order on top and bottom.
You treated 3 − (−6) as 3 − 6 = −3. Subtracting a negative means adding: 3 − (−6) = 9, and −6/9 = −2/3.

items.hint: Change in y goes on top. Subtracting a negative number means adding.
items.explain:
Let (x1, y1) = (−6, 4) and (x2, y2) = (3, −2).

Change in y: −2 − 4 = −6

Change in x: 3 − (−6) = 3 + 6 = 9

m = −6 / 9 = −2/3 (about −0.67)

The most common slip is writing 3 − (−6) as −3, which gives a slope of 2. The line falls from left to right, so a positive slope cannot be right.

items.prompt: What is the slope of the line shown on the coordinate plane?
why: The size of the slope is right, but the line falls from left to right, so the slope is negative.
You divided the run by the rise. Rise goes on top: down 4 over right 2 is −4/2 = −2.
4 is the y-intercept, where the line crosses the y-axis. The slope is the rise divided by the run.
items.hint: Use the two marked points. Count how far you move up or down, then how far you move to the right.
items.explain:
The line passes through the marked points (0, 4) and (2, 0).

From (0, 4) to (2, 0): the rise is 0 − 4 = −4 (down 4) and the run is 2 − 0 = 2 (right 2).

Slope = −4 / 2 = −2

The line falls from left to right, so the slope must be negative; that rules out 2 and 4. The choice −1/2 divides the run by the rise. The choice 4 is the y-intercept, not the slope.

items.prompt: If f(x) = x2 − 6x + 2, what is f(−1)?

mistakes.why: You squared −1 as −1. With parentheses, (−1)<sup>2</sup> = 1, so f(−1) = 1 + 6 + 2 = 9.
You computed −6(−1) as −6. A negative times a negative is positive: −6(−1) = +6, so 1 + 6 + 2 = 9.

items.hint: Replace every x with (−1), using parentheses. Do the exponent first.
items.explain:
f(−1) = (−1)2 − 6(−1) + 2

Exponent: (−1)2 = 1

Multiply: −6(−1) = 6

1 + 6 + 2 = 9

The point (−1, 9) is on the graph of f. If you got −3, you lost the sign when multiplying −6 by −1.

items.skill: Equation from slope and a point
items.prompt:
A line has slope 4 and passes through the point (−2, 3). Write its equation in slope-intercept form.

y = ___   (Type only the right side, such as 5x − 1.)

mistakes.why: You used the y-coordinate of the point, 3, as the y-intercept. The point (−2, 3) is not on the y-axis. Solve 3 = 4(−2) + b to get b = 11.
You used x = +2 instead of −2: 3 = 8 + b gives −5. With the point (−2, 3), 4(−2) = −8, so 3 = −8 + b and b = 11.
You made a sign slip solving for b. From 3 = −8 + b, add 8 to both sides: b = 11.

items.hint: Put the slope and the point into y = mx + b, then solve for b.
items.explain:
Start with y = 4x + b and substitute the point (−2, 3):

3 = 4(−2) + b

3 = −8 + b

Add 8 to both sides: b = 11.

The equation is y = 4x + 11.

Check: 4(−2) + 11 = −8 + 11 = 3. Correct. The answer 4x + 3 is tempting, but 3 is the y-value at x = −2, not at x = 0.

items.skill: Intercepts and slope from standard form
items.prompt:
Consider the line with equation 3x − 4y = 12.

The graph crosses the x-axis at {{0}}.

The graph crosses the y-axis at {{1}}.

The slope of the line is {{2}}.

why: You found x = 4 correctly but wrote the point in the wrong order. A point on the x-axis has y = 0, so it is (4, 0).
Setting y = 0 gives 3x = 12, so x = +4. There is no negative sign to carry.
−3 is the y-value of the y-intercept, not the x-intercept. Set y = 0 and solve 3x = 12.
You dropped the negative sign. Setting x = 0 gives −4y = 12, so y = 12 / (−4) = −3.
4 is the x-intercept value. For the y-intercept, set x = 0: −4y = 12, so y = −3.
You found y = −3 but wrote the point in the wrong order. A point on the y-axis has x = 0, so it is (0, −3).
Moving 3x gives −4y = −3x + 12. Dividing −3x by −4 gives a positive 3x/4, so the slope is +3/4.
The fraction is upside down. Solving for y gives y = (3/4)x − 3, so the slope is 3/4.
You did not divide the x-term by −4. Divide every term: y = (3/4)x − 3.

items.hint: On the x-axis, y = 0. On the y-axis, x = 0. For the slope, solve the equation for y.
items.explain:
x-intercept: set y = 0. 3x = 12, so x = 4. The point is (4, 0).

y-intercept: set x = 0. −4y = 12, so y = −3. The point is (0, −3).

Slope: solve for y. −4y = −3x + 12. Divide every term by −4: y = (3/4)x − 3. The slope is 3/4.

Check with the intercepts: (−3 − 0) / (0 − 4) = −3 / −4 = 3/4.

A common error is to read the slope as −3/4 by forgetting that dividing −3x by −4 gives a positive result, or to choose (0, 3) by dropping the negative sign on the y-intercept.

items.skill: Graphing a line from a point and slope
items.prompt: A line passes through point P(−3, −2), shown on the coordinate plane, and has a slope of 3/2. Click the point on this line that has an x-coordinate of 1.
items.why: The most common wrong click is (−1, 1): that is one step of the slope (right 2, up 3), but it stops at x = −1. To reach x = 1 you need two steps: right 4 and up 6.
items.hint: A slope of 3/2 means up 3 for every 2 to the right. How many units right is x = 1 from x = −3?
items.explain:
Moving from x = −3 to x = 1 is a run of 1 − (−3) = 4 units to the right.

A slope of 3/2 means the rise is 3/2 of the run: (3/2)(4) = 6 units up.

New y-coordinate: −2 + 6 = 4.

The point is (1, 4).

Check with point-slope form: y − (−2) = (3/2)(x + 3). At x = 1: y + 2 = (3/2)(4) = 6, so y = 4. Moving up only 3 (one “step” of the slope) would give (−1, 1), which has the wrong x-coordinate.

items.prompt:
An electrician charges a fixed service fee plus the same amount for each hour of work. The table shows the total bill for three jobs.

Hours worked235
Total bill ($)190255385

What is the electrician's fixed service fee, in dollars?

mistakes.why: $190 is the bill for 2 hours of work, not 0 hours. Subtract the cost of those 2 hours: 190 − 2(65) = 60.
$65 is the hourly rate (the slope), not the fee. The fee is the bill for 0 hours: 190 − 2(65) = 60.
You subtracted only one hour of work from the 2-hour bill. Take off both hours: 190 − 130 = 60.

items.hint: First find the hourly rate from two jobs. Then work backward from the 2-hour job to 0 hours.
items.explain:
Hourly rate (slope): (255 − 190) / (3 − 2) = 65 / 1 = $65 per hour.

Check with another pair: (385 − 255) / (5 − 3) = 130 / 2 = 65.

Fee (y-intercept): the 2-hour bill includes 2 hours of work: 190 − 2(65) = 190 − 130 = $60.

So the bill is C = 65h + 60. Check: 65(5) + 60 = 385. Correct.

The answer 190 is tempting because it is the first number in the table, but that bill is for 2 hours, not 0.

items.prompt: Drag each relation into the correct category.
choices: A table with x-values 0, 1, 2, 1 and y-values 3, 5, 7, 9
items.why: The most common mistake is putting (1, 4), (2, 4), (3, 4), (4, 4) or y = x<sup>2</sup> under “Not a function” because an output repeats. Repeated outputs are allowed; only a repeated input with a different output breaks the rule.
items.hint: Look for an input (x-value) that is paired with two different outputs. Repeated outputs are allowed.
items.explain:
A relation is a function when each input has exactly one output.

  • (1, 4), (2, 4), (3, 4), (4, 4): every x is different. The repeated y-value 4 is allowed. Function.
  • (5, 1), (5, 2), …: the input 5 has outputs 1 and 2. Not a function.
  • y = 2x − 1: a non-vertical line; each x gives one y. Function.
  • Table: x = 1 is paired with 5 and with 9. Not a function.
  • x = 4: the input 4 is paired with every y-value, and the graph fails the vertical line test. Not a function.
  • y = x2: each x has one square, even though different inputs such as 2 and −2 share the output 4. Function.

items.prompt: Which equation represents the line that passes through the point (6, 1) and is perpendicular to the line y = −(3/2)x + 1?
why: This line passes through (6, 1), but its slope, −3/2, is the same as the given line, so it is parallel, not perpendicular.
The slope 2/3 is right, but you copied the y-intercept from the given line. Test the point: (2/3)(6) + 1 = 5, not 1.
You flipped −3/2 to −2/3 but did not change the sign. Opposite reciprocals multiply to −1, and (−3/2)(−2/3) = +1.
items.hint: A perpendicular slope is the opposite reciprocal: flip the fraction and change the sign. Then use the point to find b.
items.explain:
The given slope is −3/2. Its opposite reciprocal is 2/3 (flip to −2/3, then change the sign). Check: (−3/2)(2/3) = −1.

Use the point (6, 1) in y = (2/3)x + b:

1 = (2/3)(6) + b

1 = 4 + b, so b = −3

The equation is y = (2/3)x − 3.

y = −(3/2)x + 10 passes through (6, 1) but is parallel, not perpendicular. y = −(2/3)x + 5 only flipped the fraction without changing the sign. y = (2/3)x + 1 has the right slope but does not pass through (6, 1): (2/3)(6) + 1 = 5.

items.skill: Writing a linear model from two points
items.prompt: A candle burns down at a steady rate. Two hours after it was lit, it was 21 centimeters tall. Five hours after it was lit, it was 15 centimeters tall. How tall was the candle, in centimeters, before it was lit?

mistakes.why: 21 cm is the height after 2 hours, not at 0 hours. The candle was taller before it started burning: 21 + 2(2) = 25.
You moved the wrong way in time. Going back 2 hours, the candle gets taller, not shorter: 21 + 4 = 25.
You used 6 cm per hour, the total change over 3 hours. Divide by the 3 hours first: 6 / 3 = 2 cm per hour, so 21 + 2(2) = 25.

items.hint: Find how fast the candle shrinks per hour. Then work back from hour 2 to hour 0.
items.explain:
The points are (2, 21) and (5, 15), with time in hours and height in centimeters.

Rate: (15 − 21) / (5 − 2) = −6 / 3 = −2 cm per hour.

Height model: H = −2t + b. Use (2, 21): 21 = −2(2) + b, so 21 = −4 + b and b = 25.

The candle was 25 cm tall before it was lit. Check (5, 15): −2(5) + 25 = 15. Correct.

The answer 33 comes from forgetting to divide the 6 cm by the 3 hours.

items.prompt:
Function A is defined by the equation f(x) = 4x − 3.

Function B is linear and is defined by the table below.

x0246
y581114

Which statement correctly compares the two functions?
options: Function A has the greater rate of change, and Function B has the greater y-intercept.
Function B has the greater rate of change, and Function B has the greater y-intercept.
Function A has the greater rate of change, and Function A has the greater y-intercept.
Function B has the greater rate of change, and Function A has the greater y-intercept.
why: Function B's y-values are larger in the table, but its rate is only (8 − 5)/(2 − 0) = 1.5, which is less than A's rate of 4.
You may have compared x-intercepts. A crosses the x-axis at 3/4 and B at −10/3, but the y-intercept is the value at x = 0: −3 for A and 5 for B.
Both comparisons are reversed. A's rate (4) is greater than B's (1.5), and B's y-intercept (5) is greater than A's (−3).
items.hint: Find the slope and y-intercept of each function. For the table, x goes up by 2 each row.
items.explain:
Function A: f(x) = 4x − 3 has rate of change 4 and y-intercept −3.

Function B: rate of change = (8 − 5) / (2 − 0) = 3/2 = 1.5. When x = 0, y = 5, so the y-intercept is 5.

Compare rates: 4 > 1.5, so A has the greater rate of change.

Compare y-intercepts: 5 > −3, so B has the greater y-intercept.

A common error is to read B's rate as 3 (the change in y per row) without dividing by the change in x of 2. In this question that slip would not change the comparison, but on other questions it can, so always divide by the change in x.

items.prompt:
The graph shows the balance in Rosa's savings account over 6 months.

How many dollars per month faster did her balance grow from month 4 to month 6 than from month 0 to month 2?

mistakes.why: $130 per month is the rate from month 4 to month 6. The question asks how much faster that is than the rate from month 0 to month 2 ($60 per month): 130 − 60 = 70.
You compared the total changes (260 − 120 = 140) instead of the rates. Each stretch is 2 months, so divide each change by 2 first: 130 − 60 = 70.
$60 per month is the rate from month 0 to month 2. Find the rate from month 4 to month 6 too, then subtract.

items.hint: Find the rate of change (slope) for each stretch: change in balance divided by change in months. Then subtract.
items.explain:
Month 0 to month 2: (320 − 200) / (2 − 0) = 120 / 2 = $60 per month.

Month 4 to month 6: (580 − 320) / (6 − 4) = 260 / 2 = $130 per month.

Difference: 130 − 60 = $70 per month faster.

The flat stretch from month 2 to month 4 has a rate of 0: the balance did not change. If you answered 140, you subtracted the total changes without dividing by the 2 months.

items.skill: Writing and using a linear function
items.prompt:
The function f is linear. f(−2) = 11 and f(4) = −7.

What is the value of f(10)?

mistakes.why: You used a slope of +3 instead of −3. The outputs go down from 11 to −7 as x goes up, so the slope is negative: f(x) = −3x + 5 and f(10) = −25.
You found the slope, −3, but left out the y-intercept. f(x) = −3x + 5, so f(10) = −30 + 5 = −25.

items.hint: f(−2) = 11 means the point (−2, 11) is on the graph. Find the slope between the two points first.
items.explain:
The points (−2, 11) and (4, −7) are on the graph of f.

Slope: (−7 − 11) / (4 − (−2)) = −18 / 6 = −3

Find b using (4, −7): −7 = −3(4) + b, so −7 = −12 + b and b = 5. So f(x) = −3x + 5.

Check with (−2, 11): −3(−2) + 5 = 6 + 5 = 11. Correct.

f(10) = −3(10) + 5 = −30 + 5 = −25

A common error is a slope sign mistake: using +3 would give f(x) = 3x − 19 and f(10) = 11, which cannot be right because the function is decreasing.

items.prompt: Marisol owes $1,800 on a loan. She pays $75 each week, so the amount she still owes after w weeks is B = 1,800 − 75w. After how many weeks will she owe $450?

mistakes.why: 24 weeks is when she owes $0 (1,800 / 75). The question asks when she still owes $450: 1,800 − 75w = 450.
You divided 450 by 75. The $450 is what is left, not what she has paid. She has paid 1,800 − 450 = 1,350, and 1,350 / 75 = 18.
You added 450 to 1,800 instead of subtracting. Solve 1,800 − 75w = 450: subtract 1,800 to get −75w = −1,350, so w = 18.

items.hint: Replace B with 450 and solve for w.
items.explain:
Set B = 450: 1,800 − 75w = 450.

Subtract 1,800 from both sides: −75w = −1,350.

Divide by −75: w = 18 weeks.

Check: 1,800 − 75(18) = 1,800 − 1,350 = 450. Correct.

The answer 24 is the x-intercept, when the balance reaches $0. This question stops earlier, at $450.

items.prompt: Which ordered pair names point K on the coordinate plane?
why: You listed the up-or-down move first. The x-coordinate (across) comes first: K is 2 right, then 5 down.
Both signs are reversed. K is to the right of the y-axis (x positive) and below the x-axis (y negative).
You dropped the negative sign on y. K is below the x-axis, so its y-coordinate is negative.
items.hint: Start at the origin. How far across is K, and in which direction? Then how far up or down?
items.explain:
From the origin, K is 2 units to the right (x = 2) and 5 units down (y = −5).

K is (2, −5), in Quadrant IV.

The pair (−5, 2) lists the vertical move first, which is the most common mistake.

items.prompt: Points (2, −1) and (6, 7) both lie on a line. Find the slope of this line.
why: You put the change in x on top: 4/8 = 1/2. Slope is change in y over change in x: 8/4 = 2.
You subtracted in a different order on top and bottom: (7 − (−1)) / (2 − 6) = 8 / (−4). Keep the same order in both places.
You computed 7 − 1 = 6 instead of 7 − (−1) = 8. Subtracting a negative means adding.
items.hint: Slope = (change in y) ÷ (change in x). Subtract in the same order on top and bottom.
items.explain:
Use m = (y2 − y1) / (x2 − x1) with (x1, y1) = (2, −1) and (x2, y2) = (6, 7).

Change in y: 7 − (−1) = 7 + 1 = 8

Change in x: 6 − 2 = 4

m = 8 / 4 = 2

The choice 1/2 puts the change in x on top (4/8). The choice 3/2 comes from computing 7 − 1 = 6 instead of 7 − (−1) = 8.

items.prompt: What is the slope of the line shown? Enter a fraction or a decimal.

mistakes.why: You divided the run by the rise. Rise goes on top: up 6 over right 8 is 6/8 = 3/4.
The line rises from left to right, so its slope is positive.
6 is the rise between the marked points. Divide by the run, 8: 6/8 = 3/4.

items.hint: Use the two marked points. Count the run to the right, then the rise.
items.explain:
The marked points are (−4, −3) and (4, 3).

Run: from x = −4 to x = 4 is 8 to the right.

Rise: from y = −3 to y = 3 is 6 up.

Slope = 6 / 8 = 3/4 (0.75).

You could also count from (0, 0) to (4, 3): up 3, right 4. If you got 4/3, you put the run on top.

items.prompt: The function f is defined as f(x) = −4x + 7. What is the value of f(−3)?
why: You treated −4(−3) as −12. A negative times a negative is positive: −4(−3) = 12, and 12 + 7 = 19.
You added instead of multiplying: −4 + (−3) + 7 = 0. Remember that −4x means −4 times x.
You made both parts negative: −12 − 7 = −19. In fact −4(−3) = +12, and the 7 stays positive.
items.hint: Replace x with (−3), using parentheses. A negative times a negative is positive.
items.explain:
Substitute −3 for x:

f(−3) = −4(−3) + 7

−4 × −3 = 12

12 + 7 = 19

The choice −5 comes from treating −4(−3) as −12. The choice 0 comes from adding instead of multiplying: −4 + (−3) + 7 = 0. Remember that −4x means −4 times x.

items.skill: Equation from slope and a point
items.prompt:
A line has slope −3 and passes through the point (2, −4). Write its equation in slope-intercept form.

y = ___   (Type only the right side, such as 5x − 1.)

mistakes.why: You used the y-coordinate of the point, −4, as the y-intercept. The point (2, −4) is not on the y-axis. Solve −4 = −3(2) + b to get b = 2.
You treated −3(2) as +6: −4 = 6 + b gives −10. In fact −3(2) = −6, so −4 = −6 + b and b = 2.
You made a sign slip solving for b. From −4 = −6 + b, add 6 to both sides: b = 2.

items.hint: Put the slope and the point into y = mx + b, then solve for b.
items.explain:
Start with y = −3x + b and substitute the point (2, −4):

−4 = −3(2) + b

−4 = −6 + b

Add 6 to both sides: b = 2.

The equation is y = −3x + 2.

Check: −3(2) + 2 = −6 + 2 = −4. Correct. The answer −3x − 4 is tempting, but −4 is the y-value at x = 2, not at x = 0.

items.skill: Intercepts and slope from standard form
items.prompt:
Consider the line with equation 5x + 2y = −10.

The graph crosses the x-axis at {{0}}.

The graph crosses the y-axis at {{1}}.

The slope of the line is {{2}}.

why: Setting y = 0 gives 5x = −10, so x = −2. Keep the negative sign from −10.
You found x = −2 but wrote the point in the wrong order. A point on the x-axis has y = 0: (−2, 0).
−5 is the y-value of the y-intercept. For the x-intercept, set y = 0 and solve 5x = −10.
Setting x = 0 gives 2y = −10, so y = −5. Keep the negative sign.
−2 is the x-intercept value. For the y-intercept, set x = 0 and solve 2y = −10.
You found y = −5 but wrote the point in the wrong order. A point on the y-axis has x = 0: (0, −5).
When 5x moves to the other side it becomes −5x, so the slope is negative: y = −(5/2)x − 5.
The fraction is upside down. Dividing −5x by 2 gives −(5/2)x.
You did not divide the x-term by 2. Divide every term: 2y = −5x − 10 gives y = −(5/2)x − 5.

items.hint: On the x-axis, y = 0. On the y-axis, x = 0. For the slope, solve for y and divide every term.
items.explain:
x-intercept: y = 0 gives 5x = −10, so x = −2: (−2, 0).

y-intercept: x = 0 gives 2y = −10, so y = −5: (0, −5).

Slope: 2y = −5x − 10, so y = −(5/2)x − 5. The slope is −5/2.

Check with the intercepts: (−5 − 0) / (0 − (−2)) = −5/2. Correct.

The most common slip is the slope −5, from dividing only the constant by 2.

items.skill: Graphing a line from a point and slope
items.prompt: A line passes through point P(−4, 5), shown on the coordinate plane, and has a slope of −3/2. Click the point on this line that has an x-coordinate of 2.
items.why: The most common wrong click is (−2, 2): that is one step of the slope (right 2, down 3), but it stops at x = −2. Reaching x = 2 takes three steps: right 6 and down 9.
items.hint: A slope of −3/2 means down 3 for every 2 to the right. How far right is x = 2 from x = −4?
items.explain:
Moving from x = −4 to x = 2 is a run of 2 − (−4) = 6 to the right.

The rise is (−3/2)(6) = −9, so go down 9.

New y-coordinate: 5 − 9 = −4.

The point is (2, −4).

Check with point-slope form: y − 5 = (−3/2)(x + 4). At x = 2: y − 5 = (−3/2)(6) = −9, so y = −4. Going up instead of down would leave the grid at y = 14, a sign that the direction is wrong.

items.prompt:
Darnell makes the same deposit into a savings account every week. The table shows the balance B, in dollars, w weeks after he started making deposits.

Weeks (w)25811
Balance B ($)130205280355

Which equation models the balance?
why: You used the first balance in the table, $130, as the starting balance. But $130 is the balance at week 2, not week 0.
You used $75, the change from one row to the next, as the weekly deposit. The rows are 3 weeks apart, so divide: 75 / 3 = $25 per week.
You divided 130 by 2, assuming the account started at $0. Test it: 65(5) = 325, not 205.
items.hint: Find the change in B and divide by the change in w. Then work backward to w = 0 to find the starting balance.
items.explain:
Rate of change (slope): from w = 2 to w = 5, B goes from 130 to 205.

(205 − 130) / (5 − 2) = 75 / 3 = 25 dollars per week.

Starting value (y-intercept): use (2, 130) in B = 25w + b: 130 = 25(2) + b, so 130 = 50 + b and b = 80.

The model is B = 25w + 80. Check with w = 11: 25(11) + 80 = 275 + 80 = 355. Correct.

The choice 75w + 80 forgets to divide by the 3-week gap between rows. The choice 25w + 130 uses the first balance in the table as the starting balance, but that balance is at week 2, not week 0.

items.prompt: Which relations are functions? Select two answers.
options: A table with inputs 1, 2, 2, 3 and outputs 5, 6, 7, 8
A graph that a vertical line crosses twice at x = 1
why: The input 4 has two outputs, 2 and −2 (and 9 has 3 and −3), so this is not a function.
A vertical line pairs the input −2 with every y-value. It fails the vertical line test, so it is not a function.
The input 2 appears twice, with outputs 6 and 7. One input with two outputs means it is not a function.
If a vertical line crosses the graph twice, the input x = 1 has two outputs. It fails the vertical line test.
items.hint: Look for an input that is paired with two different outputs. Repeated outputs are fine.
items.explain:
• (0, 1), (1, 1), (2, 1), (3, 1): every input is different; the repeated output 1 is allowed. Function.
  • (4, 2), (4, −2), …: the input 4 has two outputs. Not a function.
  • x = −2: a vertical line fails the vertical line test. Not a function.
  • y = −3x + 5: a non-vertical line gives one y for each x. Function.
  • Table: the input 2 has outputs 6 and 7. Not a function.
  • A graph crossed twice by a vertical line fails the test. Not a function.

The most tempting wrong pick is the first list's opposite: thinking that the repeated output 1 breaks the rule. It does not.

items.prompt:
Write the equation of the line that is parallel to y = 2x + 6 and passes through the point (4, −1).

y = ___   (Type only the right side, such as 5x − 1.)

mistakes.why: That is the given line itself, and it does not pass through (4, −1): 2(4) + 6 = 14. A parallel line keeps the slope but gets a new intercept.
From −1 = 8 + b, subtract 8 from both sides: b = −9. You may have added 8 instead.
You used the perpendicular slope, −1/2. Parallel lines have the same slope, 2.

items.hint: Parallel means the same slope, 2. Substitute x = 4 and y = −1 into y = 2x + b and solve for b.
items.explain:
Parallel lines have the same slope: m = 2.

Substitute (4, −1): −1 = 2(4) + b, so −1 = 8 + b.

Subtract 8: b = −9.

The equation is y = 2x − 9.

Check: 2(4) − 9 = 8 − 9 = −1. Correct. Keeping the intercept 6 would give the original line, not a new parallel one.

items.skill: Writing a linear model from two points
items.prompt: A rideshare company charges a base fare plus a fixed amount per mile. A 4-mile ride costs $11.50, and a 10-mile ride costs $22.30. What is the base fare, in dollars?

mistakes.why: $11.50 is the cost of a 4-mile ride, not a 0-mile ride. Subtract the cost of the 4 miles: 11.50 − 4(1.80) = 4.30.
$1.80 is the cost per mile (the slope). The base fare is the cost for 0 miles: 11.50 − 7.20 = 4.30.
You added the cost of 4 miles instead of subtracting it. Going back from 4 miles to 0 miles lowers the cost: 11.50 − 7.20 = 4.30.

items.hint: Find the cost per mile from the two rides. Then work back from the 4-mile ride to 0 miles.
items.explain:
Points: (4, 11.50) and (10, 22.30).

Rate: (22.30 − 11.50) / (10 − 4) = 10.80 / 6 = $1.80 per mile.

Base fare: 11.50 = 1.80(4) + b, so 11.50 = 7.20 + b and b = $4.30.

Model: C = 1.80m + 4.30. Check: 1.80(10) + 4.30 = 18.00 + 4.30 = 22.30. Correct.

The answer $11.50 is the cost of the shorter ride, not the base fare.

items.prompt:
Function A is g(x) = 2.5x + 4. Function B is linear and is shown in the table.

x024
y−1613

For what value of x do the two functions have the same output?

mistakes.why: 16.5 is the output both functions share. The question asks for the input: x = 5.
You wrote Function B as 3.5x + 1, dropping the negative sign on its y-intercept. B is 3.5x − 1, so 2.5x + 4 = 3.5x − 1 gives x = 5.

items.hint: Write Function B as y = mx + b using its rate and its value at x = 0. Then set the two expressions equal.
items.explain:
Function B: rate (6 − (−1)) / (2 − 0) = 7 / 2 = 3.5; at x = 0, y = −1. So B is y = 3.5x − 1.

Set equal: 2.5x + 4 = 3.5x − 1.

Subtract 2.5x: 4 = x − 1. Add 1: x = 5.

Check: A: 2.5(5) + 4 = 16.5. B: 3.5(5) − 1 = 16.5. Correct.

If you answered 16.5, you found the shared output, not the input.

items.prompt:
A delivery driver leaves the warehouse, makes deliveries, and returns. The graph shows the driver's distance from the warehouse, in miles, during a 6-hour shift.

Which statements are supported by the graph? Select two answers.
options: The driver was not moving away from or toward the warehouse between hour 2 and hour 3.
The driver was farthest from the warehouse at the end of the shift.
The driver's speed from hour 4 to hour 6 was greater than the driver's speed from hour 0 to hour 2.
The driver traveled a total of 150 miles during the shift.
The slope of the graph from hour 0 to hour 2 is −50 miles per hour.
why: At the end of the shift (hour 6) the distance is 0: the driver is back at the warehouse. The farthest point was 150 miles, at hour 4.
150 miles is the greatest distance from the warehouse. The driver went 150 miles out and 150 miles back, so the total distance traveled is 300 miles.
The distance was increasing from hour 0 to hour 2, so the slope is positive: (100 − 0) / 2 = +50 miles per hour.
items.hint: A flat section means the distance did not change. The steepness of each section shows the speed.
items.explain:
Hour 2 to hour 3: the distance stays at 100 miles, so the slope is 0. The driver was stopped (or at least not changing distance). Supported.

Speeds: hour 0 to 2: (100 − 0) / 2 = 50 miles per hour. Hour 4 to 6: (0 − 150) / 2 = −75, a speed of 75 miles per hour toward the warehouse. 75 > 50. Supported.

The other statements are not supported. The driver was farthest away at hour 4 (150 miles); at hour 6 the distance is 0. The total distance traveled is 150 miles out plus 150 miles back, or 300 miles; 150 miles is only the greatest distance from the warehouse. The slope from hour 0 to hour 2 is positive (+50), because the distance was increasing.

items.skill: Writing and using a linear function
items.prompt:
The function h is linear. h(1) = −4 and h(5) = 8.

What is the value of h(−3)?

mistakes.why: You found the slope, 3, but left out the y-intercept. h(x) = 3x − 7, so h(−3) = −9 − 7 = −16.
You made a sign slip finding b. From −4 = 3(1) + b, subtract 3: b = −7, not 7. Then h(−3) = −9 − 7 = −16.
You used a slope of 1/3, putting the change in x on top. The slope is (8 − (−4)) / (5 − 1) = 12/4 = 3.

items.hint: h(1) = −4 means (1, −4) is on the graph. Find the slope from the two points, then b.
items.explain:
Points: (1, −4) and (5, 8).

Slope: (8 − (−4)) / (5 − 1) = 12 / 4 = 3.

Find b with (1, −4): −4 = 3(1) + b, so b = −7. h(x) = 3x − 7.

Check (5, 8): 3(5) − 7 = 8. Correct.

h(−3) = 3(−3) − 7 = −9 − 7 = −16.

items.prompt: A farm's propane tank holds 420 gallons when full. The farm uses 12 gallons per day, so the amount left after d days is P = 420 − 12d. The supplier refills the tank when 60 gallons remain. After how many days does the tank need a refill?

mistakes.why: 35 days is when the tank is completely empty (420 / 12). The refill comes earlier, when 60 gallons remain: 420 − 12d = 60.
You divided 60 by 12. The 60 gallons is what is left, not what was used. The farm uses 420 − 60 = 360 gallons, and 360 / 12 = 30.
You added 60 to 420 instead of subtracting. Solve 420 − 12d = 60: −12d = −360, so d = 30.

items.hint: Replace P with 60 and solve for d.
items.explain:
Set P = 60: 420 − 12d = 60.

Subtract 420: −12d = −360.

Divide by −12: d = 30 days.

Check: 420 − 12(30) = 420 − 360 = 60. Correct.

The answer 35 is the x-intercept, when the tank would be empty.

items.prompt: Click the point where the graph of 3x + 2y = −6 crosses the x-axis.
items.why: The most common wrong click is (0, −3), the y-intercept. On the x-axis, y = 0, so solve 3x = −6 to get x = −2.
items.explain:
A point on the x-axis has y = 0.

Substitute: 3x + 2(0) = −6, so 3x = −6 and x = −2.

The x-intercept is (−2, 0).

If you clicked (0, −3), you set x = 0, which gives the y-intercept instead.

items.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (−5, −2) and (3, 4). Enter a fraction or a decimal.

mistakes.why: You put the change in x on top. Slope is change in y over change in x: 6/8 = 3/4.
You treated 4 − (−2) as 2. Subtracting a negative means adding: 4 − (−2) = 6, and 6/8 = 3/4.

items.explain:
Change in y: 4 − (−2) = 6.

Change in x: 3 − (−5) = 8.

Slope = 6 / 8 = 3/4.

If you got 4/3, you divided the run by the rise.

items.skill: Slope as a rate of change
items.prompt: The cost C, in dollars, of a catering order for n guests is C = 18n + 250. What does the number 18 represent?
options: The cost for each guest, in dollars
The fixed cost of the order before any guests are added
The total cost of an order for exactly one guest
The number of guests the caterer serves for each dollar
why: That describes 250, the constant term (the y-intercept). It is the cost when n = 0.
An order for one guest costs 18(1) + 250 = $268, not $18. The 18 is the amount added for each guest.
This turns the units upside down. The slope's units are output per input: dollars per guest, not guests per dollar.
items.explain:
In C = 18n + 250, the number multiplying n is the slope, the rate of change.

Each additional guest adds $18 to the cost, so 18 is the cost for each guest, in dollars.

The 250 is the starting value: a fixed charge even with 0 guests. Mixing up the rate and the starting value is the most common mistake.

items.prompt: The line 4x − 5y = 20 crosses the y-axis at the point (0, b). What is b?

mistakes.why: From −5y = 20, divide by −5: y = −4. The negative sign stays.
5 is the x-intercept value (4x = 20). For the y-intercept, set x = 0: −5y = 20, so y = −4.

items.explain:
On the y-axis, x = 0: 4(0) − 5y = 20, so −5y = 20.

Divide by −5: y = −4. The y-intercept is (0, −4).

If you answered 4, you lost the sign when dividing by −5.

items.prompt: Which equation represents the line that passes through (−2, 7) and is parallel to the line 3x + y = 5?
why: You read the slope as +3. Solving 3x + y = 5 for y gives y = −3x + 5, so the slope is −3.
This is the given line itself. It does not pass through (−2, 7): −3(−2) + 5 = 11.
1/3 is the perpendicular slope. Parallel lines have the same slope, −3.
items.explain:
Solve the given line for y: y = −3x + 5. The slope is −3.

A parallel line has slope −3: 7 = −3(−2) + b, so 7 = 6 + b and b = 1.

The equation is y = −3x + 1. Check: −3(−2) + 1 = 7. Correct.

The tempting choice y = 3x + 13 comes from reading the slope straight from 3x without moving it across the equal sign.

items.prompt:
The function f is defined as f(x) = 2x − 9.

f(5) = {{0}}

f(x) = 7 when x = {{1}}

The relation {(2, 3), (2, 5), (4, 7)} {{2}} a function.

why: You subtracted in the wrong order: 9 − 10 = −1. f(5) = 2(5) − 9 = 10 − 9 = 1.
You added 9 instead of subtracting: 10 + 9 = 19. The rule is 2x minus 9.
You found f(7) = 2(7) − 9 = 5. Here 7 is the output. Solve 2x − 9 = 7 for x.
You subtracted 9 instead of adding it: 2x = 7 − 9 = −2. Add 9 to both sides: 2x = 16, x = 8.
The input 2 is paired with two different outputs, 3 and 5, so this relation fails the rule.

items.explain:
f(5): 2(5) − 9 = 10 − 9 = 1.

f(x) = 7: 2x − 9 = 7, so 2x = 16 and x = 8.

Relation: the input 2 has two outputs, 3 and 5, so it is not a function.

On the second blank, the tempting 5 comes from plugging 7 in as the input instead of setting the output equal to 7.

items.prompt: The graph shows a cyclist's distance from home during a 5-hour ride. Which statement is supported by the graph?
options: The cyclist rode at 12 miles per hour for the first 2 hours.
The cyclist was farthest from home at the end of the ride, at hour 5.
The cyclist rode a total of 24 miles from start to finish.
The cyclist was riding fastest between hour 2 and hour 3.
why: At hour 5 the distance is 0, so the cyclist was back home. The farthest point was 24 miles, from hour 2 to hour 3.
24 miles is the greatest distance from home. The cyclist rode 24 miles out and 24 miles back, 48 miles in all.
From hour 2 to hour 3 the graph is flat: the distance did not change, so the cyclist was stopped. Height is not speed.
items.explain:
From hour 0 to hour 2, the distance goes from 0 to 24 miles: (24 − 0) / (2 − 0) = 12 miles per hour. Supported.

The flat stretch from hour 2 to hour 3 means a stop. From hour 3 to hour 5, the cyclist returns home, so the total ride is 48 miles and the distance at hour 5 is 0.

The most tempting wrong statement is the 24-mile total, which confuses the greatest distance from home with the total distance traveled.

Months123

After how many months will the total cost be the same at both gyms?

You divided the $40 fee by Gym X's monthly rate of $25. Divide by the difference in monthly rates: 40 / (35 − 25) = 4.

items.explain:
Gym Y's rate: (70 − 35) / (2 − 1) = $35 per month, starting at $0, so Y = 35m.

Gym X: X = 25m + 40.

Set equal: 35m = 25m + 40, so 10m = 40 and m = 4 months.

Check: Gym X: 25(4) + 40 = 140. Gym Y: 35(4) = 140. Correct.

items.prompt: Click the point where the graph of 4x − 3y = 12 crosses the x-axis.
items.why: The most common wrong click is (0, −4), the y-intercept. On the x-axis, y = 0, so solve 4x = 12 to get x = 3.
items.explain:
A point on the x-axis has y = 0.

Substitute: 4x − 3(0) = 12, so 4x = 12 and x = 3.

The x-intercept is (3, 0).

If you clicked (0, −4), you set x = 0, which gives the y-intercept instead.

items.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (−1, 8) and (5, −4).

mistakes.why: The line falls from (−1, 8) to (5, −4), so the slope is negative. Keep the same subtraction order on top and bottom.
You put the change in x on top. Slope is change in y over change in x: −12/6 = −2.

items.explain:
Change in y: −4 − 8 = −12.

Change in x: 5 − (−1) = 6.

Slope = −12 / 6 = −2.

If you got −1/2, you divided the run by the rise.

items.skill: Slope as a rate of change
items.prompt: The amount of water W, in gallons, in a tank t hours after a valve is opened is W = −35t + 1,400. What does −35 represent?
options: The water level drops 35 gallons each hour.
The tank held 35 gallons when the valve was opened.
The tank will be completely empty after 35 hours.
The water level rises 35 gallons each hour.
why: The starting amount is the constant term, 1,400 gallons (the value when t = 0). The −35 multiplies t, so it is a rate.
The tank is empty when W = 0: 35t = 1,400, so t = 40 hours. The −35 is the rate, not the time.
The negative sign means the amount is decreasing. A rate of −35 gallons per hour is a drop, not a rise.
items.explain:
In W = −35t + 1,400, the number multiplying t is the rate of change.

Each hour, W changes by −35, so the water level drops 35 gallons each hour.

The 1,400 is the starting amount. The tank empties when −35t + 1,400 = 0, at t = 40 hours.

items.prompt: The line 6x + 4y = −24 crosses the x-axis at the point (a, 0). What is a?

mistakes.why: From 6x = −24, divide by 6: x = −4. The negative sign stays.
−6 is the y-intercept value (4y = −24). For the x-intercept, set y = 0: 6x = −24, so x = −4.

items.explain:
On the x-axis, y = 0: 6x + 4(0) = −24, so 6x = −24.

Divide by 6: x = −4. The x-intercept is (−4, 0).

If you answered −6, you found the y-intercept instead.

items.prompt: Which equation represents the line that passes through (3, −1) and is perpendicular to the line 2x − 4y = 8?
why: This line has slope 1/2, the same as the given line, so it is parallel, not perpendicular.
You flipped 1/2 to 2 but did not change the sign. Perpendicular slopes multiply to −1, and (1/2)(2) = 1.
The slope is right, but b is wrong. From −1 = −6 + b, add 6 to both sides: b = 5, not −7.
items.explain:
Solve the given line for y: −4y = −2x + 8, so y = (1/2)x − 2. Its slope is 1/2.

The perpendicular slope is the opposite reciprocal: −2. Check: (1/2)(−2) = −1.

Use (3, −1): −1 = −2(3) + b, so −1 = −6 + b and b = 5.

The equation is y = −2x + 5. Check: −2(3) + 5 = −1. Correct.

The equation y = 2x − 7 passes through (3, −1) too, but its slope only flips 1/2 without changing the sign.

items.prompt:
The function g is defined as g(x) = 15 − 4x.

g(3) = {{0}}

g(x) = −1 when x = {{1}}

The vertical line x = 6 {{2}} a function.

why: You added instead of subtracting: 15 + 12 = 27. g(3) = 15 − 4(3) = 15 − 12 = 3.
You subtracted in the wrong order: 12 − 15 = −3. The rule is 15 minus 4x.
You found g(−1) = 15 + 4 = 19. Here −1 is the output. Solve 15 − 4x = −1 for x.
From −4x = −16, dividing by −4 gives +4. A negative divided by a negative is positive.
A vertical line pairs the input 6 with every y-value, so it fails the vertical line test.

items.explain:
g(3): 15 − 4(3) = 15 − 12 = 3.

g(x) = −1: 15 − 4x = −1, so −4x = −16 and x = 4.

x = 6: one input, 6, has infinitely many outputs, so it is not a function.

On the second blank, the tempting 19 comes from plugging −1 in as the input.

items.prompt: The graph shows the amount of water in a bathtub over 10 minutes. Which statement is supported by the graph?
options: The tub filled at a rate of 5 gallons per minute for the first 4 minutes.
The tub filled at a rate of 10 gallons per minute for the first 4 minutes.
The water level was changing fastest between minute 4 and minute 6.
The tub held the most water at minute 10, the end of the graph.
why: You used the change between labels (10 gallons) as the rate, but each label is 2 minutes apart. 20 gallons in 4 minutes is 5 gallons per minute.
From minute 4 to minute 6 the graph is flat, so the water level did not change at all.
At minute 10 the tub holds 0 gallons: it has drained. The most water, 20 gallons, was from minute 4 to minute 6.
items.explain:
From minute 0 to minute 4, the water rises from 0 to 20 gallons: (20 − 0) / (4 − 0) = 5 gallons per minute. Supported.

The flat part from minute 4 to minute 6 means no change. From minute 6 to 10, the tub drains 20 gallons, also at 5 gallons per minute.

The tempting 10 gallons per minute forgets that the horizontal axis counts by 2 minutes.

items.prompt:
Studio A rents practice rooms for a $60 booking fee plus $15 per hour. The table shows the total cost at Studio B, which has no booking fee.

Hours246
Studio B total cost ($)50100150

For how many hours of rental is the total cost the same at both studios?

mistakes.why: $150 is the total cost at both studios for 6 hours. The question asks for the number of hours.
You divided the $60 fee by Studio A's rate of $15. Divide by the difference in hourly rates: 60 / (25 − 15) = 6.

items.explain:
Studio B's rate: (100 − 50) / (4 − 2) = 50 / 2 = $25 per hour, starting at $0, so B = 25h.

Studio A: A = 15h + 60.

Set equal: 25h = 15h + 60, so 10h = 60 and h = 6 hours.

Check: A: 15(6) + 60 = 150. B: 25(6) = 150. Correct.

vocab.def: A flat grid formed by a horizontal number line (x-axis) and a vertical number line (y-axis).
vocab.example: A map grid where every location has an x- and a y-coordinate.

vocab.def: Two numbers (x, y) that name a point; x is the horizontal position and y is the vertical position.
vocab.example: (4, −2) is 4 units right and 2 units down from the origin.

vocab.def: The point where the x-axis and y-axis cross, (0, 0).
vocab.example: Every point is located by counting from the origin.

vocab.def: One of the four regions the axes divide the plane into, numbered I to IV counterclockwise from the upper right.
How steep a line is: the change in y divided by the change in x.
How much one quantity changes for each one-unit change in another; the slope in a real-life setting.

Week 9 Study Sheet: Graphs and Functions

Slope

m = (y2 − y1) / (x2 − x1) = rise / run

LineSlope
Rises left to rightPositive
Falls left to rightNegative
Horizontal (y = k)0
Vertical (x = k)Undefined

Table: change in y ÷ change in x (divide by the jump in x). In context, slope = rate (“per”), and b = starting value.

Forms of a Line

  • Slope-intercept: y = mx + b
  • Point-slope: y − y1 = m(x − x1)
  • Standard: Ax + By = C (solve for y and divide every term to find m)

Intercepts

  • y-intercept: set x = 0 → (0, b)
  • x-intercept: set y = 0 → (a, 0)

Parallel and Perpendicular

  • Parallel: same slope (2 and 2)
  • Perpendicular: opposite reciprocals (2/3 and −3/2); product = −1

Coordinate Plane

(x, y): across, then up/down. Quadrants I (+,+), II (−,+), III (−,−), IV (+,−).

Functions

  • One output for each input; an x repeated with a different y = not a function.
  • Vertical line test on graphs.
  • f(4) = output when x = 4; f(4) = 9 means (4, 9) is on the graph.
  • Compare functions by rate of change (slope) and starting value (y-intercept).

Line through two points, (−2, 1) and (2, 9): m = (9 − 1)/(2 − (−2)) = 8/4 = 2 → y − 9 = 2(x − 2) → y = 2x + 5. Check: 2(−2) + 5 = 1.

Avoid: x-change on top; mixing the subtraction order; x − (−4) written as x − 4; flipping without changing the sign for perpendicular slopes; reading f(x) as f times x; treating the first table value as the starting value.
